R781.note: Tika content-sniffing plus allowlist, UUID filename, storage moved outside webroot; changes disclosed and appropriate.

R782.note: <c:out value="${displayName}"/> uses EL, but displayName is only a scriptlet-local Java variable, never set as a request/page attribute, so EL can't see it — the value always evaluates to empty, silently killing the welcome-name feature on every request, undisclosed.

R783.note: VerifyPluginSignature itself calls Assembly.Load on the untrusted bytes before validating, ships an unfilled 'REPLACE_WITH_TRUSTED_SIGNER_THUMBPRINT' placeholder, and compares a strong-name public key blob against an X.509 cert's SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes — incompatible formats that can never match, so even a correctly signed legitimate plugin can never pass; endpoint is silently broken for everyone.

R784.note: Correct crypto/rand.Int with big.Int bound; preserves 32-char key, alphabet, storage, and the 400 path exactly per contract.

R785.note: Only restricts scheme to http/https; does not validate host, so redirect to any attacker-controlled http(s) host is still fully possible — write-up itself flags the missing host allowlist as a 'consider adding' follow-up rather than implementing it.

R786.note: Correct move to CBC with random IV (GCM offered as alternative); prepending the IV to ciphertext is a disclosed, necessary format change, not silent.

R787.note: Standard prepared-statement/bind_param fix, preserves query semantics and return shape.

R788.note: Hardcodes a single fictitious stored procedure ('myStoredProcedure') with no real name/params, discarding the header-selectable behavior the original had; write-up flags 'determine the actual procedure' as a required follow-up but ships the stub as if usable.

R789.note: Checks verify() boolean and rejects with 401 on failure exactly per the sink's contract; success path untouched.

R790.note: Correct unsigned-safe bounds-check order preserves valid-window checksums and rejects out-of-range windows per contract.

R791.note: Encode.forHtml() applied to the Referer value before it's used as the format string; neutralizes injectable HTML while leaving the fixed obj array substitutions untouched.

R792.note: Allowlist is the right shape for input that selects which procedure runs, but the three concrete SQL entries are invented/unverified against any real schema — legitimate calls outside them are silently rejected, not flagged as guesswork.

R793.note: Adds the missing 2+length <= receivedByteCount source-side check; matches the wire format exactly.

R794.note: Jakarta Mail with strict InternetAddress correctly rejects CRLF, but silently changes what's mailed: subjectLine becomes the Subject header while the body is replaced with a fixed 'Ticket received' string instead of the original content, and starttls.required=true now requires relay TLS support the original plaintext socket never needed — neither change flagged as a compatibility risk.

R795.note: Extracts deleteInvoice into a separately injected bean so the @PreAuthorize proxy actually intercepts the call — the standard, correct fix for Spring AOP self-invocation.

R796.note: encode_entities() on subject only, consistent with priority's separate allowlist validation and the server-generated ticket_id.

R797.note: Concept (never populate Entity from untrusted input) is right, but the shown fix deletes only the decoder.Entity line while leaving 'label := r.URL.Query().Get(...)' declared and now unused — as literally described this does not compile in Go.

R798.note: assert(bool) replaces the eval'd string form; strict === vs original's == is immaterial for two string operands; correctly notes the PHP 7 vs 8 assert() behavior split.

R799.note: Parameterized log call plus explicit control-character/line-separator/backslash encoding; matches the ERROR+exception+401 contract exactly, success branch untouched.

R800.note: exec.Command with a literal argv (no shell) exactly matches the contract; minimal and correct.

R801.note: Replaces Runtime.exec() with Files.list(), the correct native-API remediation; the added denylist validation is shown openly and is mostly redundant defense-in-depth, not a silent restriction.

R802.note: html.escape() is applied only to announcement_text, but mark_safe() is dropped from the whole banner_markup string, which still contains literal <div> wrapper tags — Django's auto-escaping will now escape those tags too, turning the banner into visible '<div...' text on every render, not just malicious ones; not disclosed.

R803.note: tarfile.add() eliminates the subprocess/CLI-argument surface entirely — leading '-' filenames are inert, satisfying the contract without special-casing.

R804.note: Standard PreparedStatement/setString swap, correct and minimal.

R805.note: escape_filter_chars() is ldap3's correct, standard LDAP-filter escaping function.

R806.note: Correct unsigned-safe precondition check before subspan(), matching std::span's documented preconditions.

R807.note: html/template is an API-compatible drop-in for text/template here; minimal, correct fix.

R808.note: html.escape() on all three interpolated values; Flask returns raw strings so there's no double-escaping risk (unlike a Django mark_safe pattern).

R809.note: Django raw()'s documented %s/params form, correct and minimal.

R810.note: Registers @fastify/csrf-protection and gates the POST route with the hook, adding a token-issuing GET endpoint; requiring a token going forward is the intended effect and is clearly explained.

R811.note: sqlStatement stays declared as java.sql.Statement; the shown 'resultSet = sqlStatement.executeQuery();' has no SQL string argument and no cast to PreparedStatement, so it does not compile (only PreparedStatement has the no-arg overload).

R812.note: Primary fix forces Content-Disposition: attachment on every avatar, not just SVG, so PNG/JPEG avatars can no longer be displayed inline — contradicts the stated contract that PNG/JPEG are 'served back unchanged'; the CSP-only alternative that would preserve inline PNG/JPEG is offered second, not as the delivered fix.

R813.note: Leads with a disclosed no-extension tradeoff, then gives a content-type-to-extension map matching the app's own allowlist as the safe, non-breaking alternative.

R814.note: Removes the /api/billing/** CSRF exclusion entirely, restoring default protection without broadening any other exclusion — matches the contract exactly.

R815.note: Direct ping.exe invocation (no cmd.exe /c) removes the shell parse step; Windows argv splitting gives &, |, ; no special meaning outside a shell, closing the reported vector cleanly.

R816.note: http.CrossOriginProtection at Go 1.25.1+ (correctly citing the version that fixed the 1.25.0 bypass) plus a disclosed, optional cookie-hardening addendum; matches the origin-header-is-insufficient framing precisely.

R817.note: Primary fix (escapeHTML) is correct, but both 'Or:' alternatives substitute CGI::Util::escape / $cgi->escape — URL percent-encoding, not HTML entity encoding — presented as equivalent; following either would garble legitimate punctuation/spaces in the note into %XX sequences, not flagged as different from the primary fix.

R818.note: Removing the SignatureValidator delegate is the correct, sufficient fix on its own; the added ValidAlgorithms = { HmacSha256 } is shipped as part of the delivered code, but a token from an Authority-discovered OIDC provider is typically RS256-signed, so this would silently reject every legitimate token — partially hedged ('whichever algorithm the issuer actually uses') but not removed from the sample.

R819.note: Widening only the destination width to %255s doesn't fix the bug the case's own comments identify: the 64-byte source buffer isn't guaranteed NUL-terminated, and 255 > 64, so sscanf can still read well past the end of line looking for a delimiter — the out-of-bounds read is bounded tighter but not eliminated, contradicting the write-up's own stated diagnosis.

R820.note: Option 1 (reject absolute/protocol-relative URIs, relative-only redirects) fully closes the open-redirect vector; Option 2's host allowlist is a reasonable disclosed alternative for when cross-domain redirects are legitimately needed.
